Baden-Baden|Germany.f: The Romans called its hot springs Aquae, and in 2021 the town joined the UNESCO Great Spa Towns of Europe.

Erfurt|Germany.f: Erfurt's Old Synagogue, built in 1094, is the oldest intact synagogue in Europe and became a UNESCO site in 2023.

Kassel|Germany.f: Kassel became the first city in the world lit by laser beams at night, during documenta 6 in 1977.

Weeze|Germany.f: The town lost 400 jobs when RAF Laarbruch closed in 1999, then turned the airbase into an airport that opened in 2003.

Friedrichshafen|Germany.f: The 128 m LZ1 airship rose from its mooring here on 2 July 1900, starting Zeppelin's airship story.

Paderborn|Germany.f: Pharmacist's apprentice Friedrich Sertuerner first isolated morphine from opium in Paderborn in 1804.

Rostock|Germany.f: Founded in 1419, the University of Rostock is the oldest university in continental northern Europe.

Cuxhaven|Germany.f: The last Enigma-encrypted message of WWII was sent from Cuxhaven on 7 May 1945, ending with Closing down for ever.

Heringsdorf|Germany.f: Until 2006 the resort municipality was officially named Dreikaiserbaeder, meaning Three Imperial Spas.

Sylt|Germany.f: Sylt has only been an island since the Grote Mandrenke flood of 1362.

Lübeck|Germany.f: With six church towers over 100 metres, Lubeck has more of them than any other city in the world.

Saarbrücken|Germany.f: Saarbruecken twice split from Germany, as capital of the Saar Basin from 1920 to 1935 and of the Saar Protectorate from 1947 to 1956.

Mannheim|Germany.f: Karl Drais built the first two-wheeled draisine, the first bicycle, in Mannheim in 1817.

Emden|Germany.f: The 1571 Synod of Emden is generally considered the founding of the Dutch Reformed Church.

Borkum|Germany.f: Wernher von Braun launched the two A2 rocket prototypes Max and Moritz from Borkum in December 1934.

Norderney|Germany.f: In 1797 Norderney became the first German resort on the North Sea.

Wangerooge|Germany.f: Wangerooge was the only East Frisian island that belonged to the Grand Duchy and Free State of Oldenburg from 1815 to 1947.

Norddeich|Germany.f: Norden, which includes Norddeich, hosts the launch point of the SEA-ME-WE 3 submarine cable, billed as the world's longest.

Büsum|Germany.f: On 4 May 1945, the last day of war in northern Germany, Busum was bombed.

Juist|Germany.f: Juist banned most motor vehicles, so only the fire department, Red Cross and doctors may drive on the island.

Helgoland|Germany.f: Werner Heisenberg retreated to Heligoland in 1925 to escape hay fever and conceived the basis of quantum theory there.

Baltrum|Germany.f: Baltrum is the smallest East Frisian island, a car-free place where horse-drawn carriages carry passengers and freight.
